1.w: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with gladness, and look on the good!” And behold, this also [is] vapor.

2.w: Of laughter, I said, “It is madness,” and of joy, “What [is] this accomplishing?”

3.w: I searched in my heart to draw out my flesh with wine, and my heart was guiding me in wisdom, and to lay hold on folly, until that I might see where [is] this good for the sons of man, that they [might] do under the heavens the number of the days of their lives.

4.w: I made great my works; I built for myself houses, and I planted for myself vineyards;

5.w: I made for myself gardens and parks, and I planted in them a tree of every fruit.

6.w: I made for myself pools of water, to cause to drink from them a grove of sprouting trees.

7.w: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and sons of the house were unto me; also there were unto me great possessions of cattle and sheep, more than all who were before my face in Jerusalem;

8.w: I gathered for myself also silver and gold, and the property of kings and of the provinces; I appointed for myself male singers and female singers, and the delights of the sons of man—a wife and wives.

9.w: So I became great, and I added more than all who were before my face in Jerusalem. Also, my wisdom stood with me.

10.w: And all that my eyes asked, I did not lay aside from them; I did not withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced in all my toil—and this was my portion from all my toil.

11.w: And I turned to all the works that my hands had done, and to the toil that I had toiled to do, and behold—all [was] vapor and a striving after the wind, and there was no profit under the sun.

12.w: And I turned to look at wisdom and madness and folly. For what [is] the man who comes after the king—that which already they have done!

13.w: And I saw that there is profit to wisdom above folly, like the profit of the light over the darkness.

14.w: The wise one, his eyes [are] in his head, and the fool is walking in the darkness. And I also knew of that event—the one that happens to all of them.

15.w: And I said in my heart, “As it happens to the fool, it will also happen to me. Then what [is] profit to me [in] being wise?” And I said in my heart, “This also [is] vapor.”

16.w: For there is no memory of the wise with the fool, forever, in that already in the days that are coming all will be forgotten. And how a wise one will die like the fool!

17.w: And I have hated this life, because the work [was] evil to me that was done under the sun—for all [is] vapor and a striving after the wind.

18.w: And I hated all my toil that I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who will come after me.

19.w: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? And he will rule over all my toil that I have toiled, and that I have done wisely, under the sun. This also [is] vapor.

20.w: And I turned around my heart to despair over all the toil that I have toiled under the sun.

21.w: For there is a man whose toil [is] with wisdom and with knowledge and with skill, and to a man not having toiled for it he must give his portion. This also [is] vapor and a great evil.

22.w: For what has been for the man for all his toil and for the striving of his heart, with which he toils under the sun?

23.w: For all his days are pains, and anger [is] his task; even in the night his heart will not find rest. This also is vapor.

24.w: Nothing [is] better for the man than to eat and drink, and his soul to see good in his toil. This also I saw, that it [is] from the hand of God;

25.w: for who can eat, and who can enjoy, apart from Him?

26.w: For to the man who [is] good in His eyes, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy; and to the sinner He gives the task to gather and to heap up, to give to the good before the face of God. This also [is] vapor, and a striving after the wind.
